headline: US stocks closed higher with Nasdaq leading as AI-driven gains in SpaceX and Super Micro lifted tech while energy eased on heating oil reserve loan plans ahead of Thursday’s data
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) finished up 0.58% at 7,757.17, rising from 7,712.57, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) also advanced and the Russell 2000 (IWM) added about 0.28% with tech outperforming and healthcare supporting the market.
- The U.S. Energy Department said it would loan heating oil (@HO) from federal reserves, contributing to weakness in energy shares during the session.
- SpaceX (SPCX) gained over 7% after reporting Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% year over year and above roughly $12.7 billion in estimates, with net income of $4.4 billion, EPS of $0.35 beating by $0.19, and Elon Musk confirming SpaceX and Tesla boards formed independent special committees to explore a potential merger.
- Super Micro Computer (SMCI) rose 9.8% to $35.66 after raising fiscal Q1 2027 revenue guidance to $18.5–$19.5 billion versus $14.9 billion consensus and lifting its gross margin outlook to 12–12.5% on strong AI server demand.
- Netflix (NFLX) fell around 5% after its Q4 revenue forecast missed estimates and it cut 2026 ad revenue guidance below expectations.
- 3M (MMM) gained about 2% after announcing a $0.5 billion optical-connectivity investment under an expanded AWS data-center collaboration with Amazon (AMZN).
- Tesla (TSLA) traded higher into its post-close earnings release after Tesla and SpaceX boards formed independent committees to explore a merger, while Meta (META) advanced in extended trading following its results and outlook.
- No major economic data moved markets on Wednesday, with investors instead looking ahead to additional reports and earnings from Lam Research (LRCX) due today after market close.
